pr_title: Allow user input for git fetch in repo sync
pr_body:
This PR modifies `repo sync` to forward IO streams to the `git fetch` command.  

Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/4295

issue_context.title: gh repo sync is broken - hangs
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Running `gh repo sync` in a freshly cloned repository hangs

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Clone a repository
Change directory into it
run `gh repo sync`

Nothing happens.  There is a text spinner `⣽` and nothing else.


### Expected vs actual behavior

Expect it to do not much at all since it is a freshly cloned repo
comments:
Thank you for reporting.

Does this happen on every attempty? If you do `DEBUG=api gh repo sync`, does it print more information about where the operation is stuck? Please share relevant parts of the output here—you may omit private information like repository names 🙇

I have given up on it
I have things to do and since `gh` does not work for me I am back to pure git
Okay! Until there are some more reproducibility steps, I am going to close this issue.

@mislav FWIW, I think the problem is that the OP saw only the "text spinner ⣽" and what is really happening is that its waiting for the passphrase, but that doesn't actually show the text.  So I think it is an open issue.

I just experienced this now with gh 2.0.0 running through xfce4-terminal on MX Linux 19 (Debian 10).

If you smack ENTER and few times, it will give you an exit status 128 and it will show that it attempted to print "_Enter passphrase for key ..._ " while all you actually see is ⣽ keeps spinning.

Entering the passphrase while ⣽ is up makes the sync complete no problem.

@mislav I got a branch that will fix this issue and forward the IO streams to the fetch operation but I am also wondering if you think it is necessary since GitHub no longer supports username/password authentication for `git` operations?

@samcoe It's a good idea to forward IO streams to any underlying process that touches the network or might trigger git hooks. In this case, the user wasn't being prompted for username/password authentication, but for their SSH passphrase. Furthermore, even if they got prompted for username/password, they could always paste a PAT in place of a password.

review_comments: Adding the IOStreams to the `gitExecuter` felt cleaner than passing it as an argument to `Fetch`.
